evidence: createApp registers Express routes (app.post/app.get/app.patch) and the express.json() middleware: this is transport, which belongs in infrastructure.
All business operations go through service.addProduct, service.placeOrder, service.listOrders, service.progressOrder and service.cancelOrder in the application layer.
orderView and productView only map domain objects to response objects.
The error middleware maps DomainError codes to HTTP 404, 409 or 400, and anything else to 500: this is transport-level error translation.
The default parameter new OrderService(new InMemoryProductRepository(), new InMemoryOrderRepository()) is composition wiring, which is acceptable in infrastructure.
The checks against fulfilmentStates and isRecord are input-shape validation for requests, not domain rules.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-server.ts is an HTTP adapter, and everything it does is infrastructure work. It sets up Express routes and body parsing, checks the shape of incoming requests, turns domain objects into response views, maps DomainError codes to HTTP status codes, and wires the default composition with the in-memory repositories. The state check in GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state compares input against the domain's fulfilmentStates list. It doesn't define any business rule itself. The actual order rules (placing, progressing and cancelling orders, and stock reservation) are handed off to OrderService. The file doesn't calculate stock, decide transitions or access persistence directly. Throwing DomainError for input that fails validation is a minor style choice, not a responsibility that belongs to another layer. No ADR prose was provided.
